title: Compliance Reporting Pack v1 — Draft Outline (Retention Controls + Audit Logging)
content:
Status: WIP outline / placeholder text. This doc is the working draft for what becomes the “Compliance Reporting Pack v1” that Sales/SE can send to enterprise prospects and that we can reuse internally for SOC 2 / ISO-aligned evidence collection.

Primary goal of this pack (v1):
- Make our data retention posture (what we retain, how long, how it’s configurable, how it’s enforced) easy to explain.
- Make audit log coverage + export story easy to explain.
- Provide a control-to-evidence matrix that maps the above to common SOC 2 / ISO27001-ish expectations.
- Provide a repeatable evidence collection procedure so the pack is not “hand-assembled” each time.

Non-goals (v1):
- Claim full custom retention across every log stream (we need to be explicit about what’s “eligible” vs governed by SRE/vendor constraints).
- Document every single product/security control at Redwood (this is a focused pack: retention + audit logging + enforcement evidence).

Audience(s):
1) Enterprise security reviewers (InfoSec questionnaires)
2) Procurement/legal (contract retention language, audit log export commitments)
3) Internal GRC/audit prep (evidence collection + traceability)

Open question up front: Do we ship one combined PDF, or a zip with multiple artifacts? (Some customers want a single PDF; others prefer a zip with “Evidence Index” + raw evidence excerpts.)

------------------------------------------------------------------------------
DRAFT PACK OUTLINE (v1)
------------------------------------------------------------------------------

0. Cover Page
- Document title: “Redwood Inference — Retention Controls & Audit Logging: Compliance Reporting Pack (v1)”
- Version + date
- Prepared for: [Customer Name] (optional placeholder)
- Contact: security@ (TBD) + Solutions contact

1. Executive Summary (1–2 pages)
- What Redwood offers: Hosted API / Dedicated / Private
- Summary of retention controls (tenant-configurable where supported)
- Summary of audit logging (admin + security-relevant events) and export options
- High-level enforcement approach (TTL where possible + scheduled deletion jobs where needed; legal hold override)
- “Limits / exclusions” (explicitly say some infra logs are governed by SRE standards/vendor retention; raw inference payload content not included in v1 scope)

PLACEHOLDER language (needs legal review):
- “Retention settings apply to Redwood-managed datasets as described in Section 4. Some infrastructure logs are retained per our operational requirements and vendor limits.”

2. Product & Deployment Scope
2.1 Deployment modes
- Hosted API
- Dedicated
- Private (VPC/on-prem)

2.2 Shared definitions
- Tenant / Organization
- Data residency vs retention (call out the difference)
- “Eligible dataset” definition (for customer-configurable retention)
- Regions / environments: prod vs staging vs dev

2.3 Data types included in v1 scope (tentative list)
- Audit logs (admin activity + security-relevant events)
- Admin activity logs (if separate from audit logs)
- Inference request metadata (NOT payload content) — TBD
- Telemetry/analytics tables (eligible subset only)
- Operational logs (selected datasets only)

TODO: Align exact dataset list with the “data inventory & retention sources” sheet + what Telemetry team is comfortable making externally-facing.

3. Retention Controls — Product Overview
3.1 How retention is configured
- Console: Retention Settings page (screenshot placeholder)
- API: retention policy endpoints (placeholder; reference to docs once stable)
- Precedence: org/tenant/env/region overrides (to confirm exact precedence rules)

3.2 Defaults by product/tier (PLACEHOLDER)
- Hosted: default retention = [X days] for audit logs, [Y days] for request metadata, etc.
- Dedicated: default retention = [X days], configurable within guardrails
- Private: customer-managed storage may control additional retention; Redwood components honor configured policy where applicable

Open questions:
- What are the intended default values by tier? (I’ve heard 30/90/365 as common asks in calls, but we need official defaults and min/max guardrails.)
- Do we allow “never delete”? Current product direction says “never delete” is disallowed unless explicitly permitted. Need crisp language.

3.3 Guardrails (min/max retention)
- Minimum retention: [N days] (rationale: security investigations + operational needs)
- Maximum retention: [M days] (rationale: storage + risk; plus some backends)
- Per dataset differences: audit logs likely have different min/max than telemetry

3.4 Legal hold and exceptions
- Legal hold semantics: overrides deletion for specified datasets/tenants
- How holds are created/approved
- How holds are visible/auditable in Console

TODO: Add a short “How to request legal hold” paragraph w/ internal process reference (customer-facing version should say “via Support / CSM”).

4. Retention Enforcement & Technical Implementation Summary (customer-friendly)
Goal: Explain “we don’t just store a config; we actually enforce it and can prove it.”

4.1 Enforcement mechanisms (high-level)
- TTL-at-storage (partition TTL where supported)
- Scheduled deletion jobs for stores without native TTL or where TTL is insufficient
- Hybrid approach depending on datastore

4.2 Safety and auditability
- Idempotent deletion jobs
- Rate limits / batch sizes to avoid DB load spikes
- Monitoring/alerting for lag/backlog/error rates
- “Effective policy” view in Console + last enforcement run timestamp

4.3 Proving behavior (what we can show)
- Screenshots of effective policy + enforcement status
- Sample audit event for “retention policy changed”
- Metrics excerpt (delete throughput, lag)
- Test strategy summary (golden tests for precedence, determinism)

Open questions:
- How much do we want to disclose about internal architecture? Enough to satisfy reviewers, not so much it becomes a security disclosure.
- Are we comfortable sharing anonymized dashboard screenshots? (SRE to confirm.)

5. Audit Logging Coverage & Retention
5.1 What gets logged
- Admin events (e.g., login, MFA changes, role/permission changes, API key actions)
- Retention policy changes
- Access to audit logs / exports
- Other security-relevant actions (TBD list)

5.2 Retention of audit logs
- Default retention
- Configurable range
- How retention applies to exported logs

5.3 Audit log exports + integrations
- Export formats (JSON/CSV) — confirm
- SIEM integration options (if any)
- Export constraints: exports limited to within retention window; metadata included if export truncated by retention

Open questions:
- For Private: do customers export from their own storage directly, or via Redwood service? Need crisp explanation.
- Do we have a “maximum export window” limit independent of retention?

6. Control-to-Evidence Matrix (SOC 2 / ISO-aligned)
This should be a table. In v1 we can anchor to common control themes rather than claim full coverage.

Table columns (draft):
- Control area (e.g., Log retention, Audit logging, Change management for security settings)
- Control statement (plain English)
- Redwood implementation summary
- Evidence artifact(s)
- Evidence location (system/source)
- Owner
- Verification steps
- Frequency / cadence

We should explicitly include:
- Retention policy configuration + approval/audit trail
- Enforcement job execution evidence
- Monitoring/alerting evidence
- Audit log coverage evidence

7. Evidence Appendix (what we can attach)
7.1 Evidence Index
- List of included artifacts + timestamp

7.2 Sample artifacts (placeholders)
- Screenshot: Console effective policy view
- Screenshot: enforcement status (last run, success/failure, exceptions)
- Redacted audit event entries for: policy update, legal hold created, export initiated
- Dashboard screenshot: lag/backlog/error rate

7.3 System description excerpts (minimal)
- One-paragraph explanation of retention enforcement architecture

Open question:
- What counts as “customer-shareable” evidence vs “internal-only”? Olga/Legal to confirm.

8. How to Generate / Update This Pack (INTERNAL RUNBOOK SECTION)
Note: For the external pack, this section may be omitted. Internally we need it.

Draft steps:
1) Confirm customer + deployment mode(s)
2) Pull current effective retention policy from control plane (per tenant)
3) Pull last enforcement run status + metrics snapshot
4) Export audit log coverage summary (or attach standard statement)
5) Assemble the PDF/zip with version stamp and “as of” date

Desired end state: script/service (ENG-2940) generates a zip:
- /pack.pdf
- /evidence-index.csv
- /screenshots/
- /snapshots/ (json exports)

------------------------------------------------------------------------------
PLACEHOLDER LINKS / EVIDENCE SOURCES (work-in-progress)
------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Confluence pages (canonical references):
- Retention controls overview: security-and-compliance/data-residency-and-retention/retention-controls-overview
- Retention policy schema/evaluation (likely too technical for customer pack; but useful internally): security-and-compliance/data-residency-and-retention/retention-policy-schema-and-evaluation
- Audit log retention + exports: security-and-compliance/audit-logging/audit-log-retention-and-exports
- Control mapping: security-and-compliance/compliance-evidence/control-mapping-retention-and-audit-logging
- Retention exceptions/legal holds process: security-and-compliance/risk-and-exceptions/retention-exceptions-and-legal-holds-process
- Enforcement runbook: eng-platform/runbooks/retention-enforcement-job-runbook
- Monitoring plan: eng-sre/reliability-initiatives/monitoring-for-retention-enforcement

Tickets / workstreams:
- PM initiative: PM-482
- Pack generator: ENG-2940
- Audit log retention worker: ENG-2920
- Telemetry retention: ENG-2921
- Legal hold flags: ENG-2934

Customer signal / requests to reference (internal):
- Jira SUP-4831 (configurable retention controls + evidence)
- Jira SUP-4870 (request for compliance report)

------------------------------------------------------------------------------
NOTES / OPEN ITEMS (as of 2025-02-18)
------------------------------------------------------------------------------

1) Defaults + guardrails
- Need final defaults by dataset + tier and min/max guardrails. Naomi to confirm with Product + Eng + GRC.

2) Dataset list for v1
- We need a crisp list that matches what we actually enforce. Avoid promising “all operational logs.”

3) “Inference request metadata” definition
- We need consistent language: what fields are included (timestamps, model, token counts, latency) vs excluded (prompt/completion content).

4) Private deployment nuances
- Private likely has the most questions: where does data live, what Redwood controls vs customer controls.

5) Evidence sharing policy
- For screenshots / dashboards: decide if we ship real screenshots, sanitized sample screenshots, or text-only attestations.

6) Packaging
- Preferred output: PDF + optional zip. Need to align with internal support request for a standard export (INT-912 mentioned in Slack; not linked here yet).

7) Legal review
- Add disclaimers: “This document is provided for informational purposes and does not modify contractual terms.” (Sofia/Michael to review.)

Next steps (owner = Daniel):
- Turn outline into a first “draft with tables” (mostly filled) by end of week.
- Sync with Olga on control mapping table format + what evidence is acceptable to share.
- Sync with Marissa/Console team on what screenshots will exist in v1 and what labels/copy should say.
- Create a placeholder Evidence Index template (csv) and standardize artifact naming.

Questions for next sync:
- What do we call this externally: “Compliance Reporting Pack” vs “Retention & Audit Logging Report”? Sales feedback suggests “report” lands better.
- Do we include a 1-page “FAQ” at the end (common reviewer Qs: legal hold, deletion guarantees, backups, vendor logs, export limits)?
